activeEvents.title: Boast the Coast Maritime Festival
activeEvents.description: Free canal-side maritime festival kicking off Lewes Maritime Weekend: Freedom Boat Club canal tours, live music from Jgar, kids' entertainment, free admission to the Cannonball House, and a paid one-hour narrated history cruise with Cape Water Tours.
activeEvents.editorialNote: Pairs naturally with Coast Day the next morning — a genuine Lewes maritime weekend.

activeEvents.title: Coast Day — 50th Anniversary
activeEvents.description: The University of Delaware's coastal, marine, and environmental science open house marks its 50th anniversary at the Hugh R. Sharp Campus, with hands-on activities, live demonstrations, and lab and ship tours. A fifth-grade essay contest on 'Habitats and Ecosystems of Delaware' accepts entries through Oct. 9.
activeEvents.venue: University of Delaware Hugh R. Sharp Campus, 700 Pilottown Rd.
activeEvents.sourceOrg: University of Delaware College of Earth, Ocean & Environment
activeEvents.editorialNote: The 50th anniversary is this issue's lead. The Lewes Chamber calendar lists 10 a.m.–3 p.m.; UD's page did not print hours, so confirm before publishing times.

dailySlots.headline: A Lewes maritime weekend anchors this week
dailySlots.note: Boast the Coast on Saturday and Coast Day's 50th anniversary on Sunday give Lewes back-to-back reasons to head to the canal and the Hugh R. Sharp Campus. Rehoboth and Dewey run their Fall Sidewalk Sale the same weekend, and the Cape Henlopen Hawk Watch keeps running daily through November.

dailySlots.headline: Look up: hawk migration is underway at the Point
dailySlots.note: Cape Henlopen's fall hawk watch runs Sept. 1 through Nov. 30, with a professional raptor counter on site most days alongside Sussex Bird Club volunteers. No experience needed to stop and watch, and the running counts are posted at hawkcount.org.

dailySlots.headline: The hull beneath Cape Henlopen: HMS DeBraak
dailySlots.note: The recovered hull of the DeBraak, an 18th-century British warship lost off Lewes, is kept at a conservation facility near Cape Henlopen State Park. The Division of Historical and Cultural Affairs runs free 'Walk to the DeBraak' tours for up to 18 visitors ages 10 and up, pairing the hull with the ship's history and crew. Check the Zwaanendael Museum for the next tour date.

dailySlots.headline: Fall surf-fishing access, explained
dailySlots.note: With Labor Day past, the summer reservation system for beach-driving at Cape Henlopen and Delaware Seashore has lifted — no reservation needed at Gordon's Pond, Herring Point, Navy Crossing, Point Crossing or 3 Rs. A surf-fishing vehicle permit is still required year-round, along with a shovel, jack, tow rope, support board and low-pressure tire gauge; beach speed limit is 15 mph.

dailySlots.headline: Sidewalk sales bookend the coast this weekend
dailySlots.note: Lewes merchants and the Rehoboth–Dewey resort area both run fall sidewalk sales Oct. 2–4, and Delaware Botanic Gardens in Dagsboro offers guided Welcome Walks at 10 a.m. on Oct. 2 and 3.

dailySlots.headline: Fifty years of Coast Day
dailySlots.note: Coast Day turns 50 this year. The University of Delaware opens its Lewes campus for hands-on marine science, live demonstrations, and lab and ship tours. Fifth graders can still enter the essay contest on Delaware's habitats and ecosystems through Oct. 9.

reviewNotes: Long-form opportunity: Delaware confirmed its third case of Chronic Wasting Disease in deer in central Sussex County this month, with DNREC holding a Sept. 16 community meeting in Georgetown on emergency hunting-season regulations. This is a genuine, fast-moving Sussex County wildlife-management story that deserves its own carefully fact-checked feature rather than a daily-slot summary — regulatory specifics should be sourced directly from DNREC's Division of Fish & Wildlife before publishing anything beyond 'a meeting was held.' Source: https://dnrec.delaware.gov/newsroom/

Long-form opportunity: DNREC's August 2026 addition of the 180-foot Calcasieu Pass to the Del-Jersey-Land artificial reef site (Reef Site 13) is a strong maritime/conservation feature — the ship's own history (built 1982 as an oilfield supply vessel, later ran three decades as an Atlantic menhaden processing ship out of Reedville, VA) gives it real narrative texture beyond a routine reef-expansion note. Source: https://news.delaware.gov/2026/08/18/latest-dnrec-artificial-reef-addition-is-180-foot-retired-oil-field-supply-ship-turned-commercial-fishing-vessel/
